subject: Mutual Action Plan: sandbox commissioning & connectivity milestones
summary: Agreement on MAP milestones for POC sandbox commissioning: org creation, API key provisioning, IP allowlist, VPC peering window, and 2-week acceptance timeline.
messages:
From: Sana Patel <sana.patel@orchidhealth.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: orchid-eng@orchidhealth.com
Date: Wed, 8 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC next steps — MAP and connectivity items

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team is excited to validate latency and cost on our clinical inference workload. Can we lock down a short Mutual Action Plan for the sandbox environment? High-level asks from Infra: org/account setup we can control, API key/service account provisioning, an IP allowlist for our egress proxies, and VPC peering so we can test streaming with minimal NAT traversal.

Can your team propose a tight timeline and any docs/templates we should fill in? Prefer an initial window the week of 4/13.

Also attaching our internal network team contact: orchid-eng@orchidhealth.com.

Thanks,
Sana
Director of Integrations
Orchid Health

[Attachment: orchid_network_requirements.pdf (stub)]

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Sana Patel <sana.patel@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 8 Apr 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC next steps — MAP and connectivity items

Sana — thanks for the note and great meeting. I sketched a short MAP that maps to your asks; see below. I attached a spreadsheet template (orchid_map_v1.xlsx) and a VPC peering YAML we typically use to accelerate networking teams.

Proposed MAP (high level)
- Day 0 (this week): Confirm org name + invite list; fill SPoC fields in the MAP spreadsheet.
- Day 1–2: Redwood creates org placeholder and issues a scoped API key for sandbox (read/write tokens limited to sandbox model).
- Day 3–4: Orchid to confirm IP allowlist CIDRs (we provide expected Redwood egress ranges) and accept VPC peering request; network validation window opens.
- Day 5–10: Smoke tests: model latency/throughput, KV cache behavior, streaming stability.
- Day 11–14: Acceptance review, sign-off, and optional rollback to smaller batch if quality regressions appear.

Technical notes / requirements
- API keys: We'll provision a single service-key with tagging for your project. Service-key rotation policy: 30 days (we can extend).
- Org setup: We'll invite two Orchid admin users (email addresses you confirm) plus one service account.
- IP allowlist: Provide CIDRs for both your test agents and our peering egress. If you need static egress, we can route traffic via a fixed NAT gateway in us-west-2.
- VPC peering: We'll initiate request from Redwood side — need your VPC name, project/account ID, and preferred CIDR. Typical acceptance time after request: 24–72 hours depending on your change freeze.

Attachments: orchid_map_v1.xlsx (MAP template), network_peering_template.yaml (peering request sample).

Next steps
1) Sana: confirm org name + 2 admin emails by EOD Friday 4/10.
2) Orchid infra: share VPC/project details and preferred peering window (we tentatively requested 4/14–4/15).
3) Redwood: we’ll provision the sandbox org + service key once we have the invite list.

Ping me if you'd like to shift the dates. I can involve Marissa for any deeper network troubleshooting.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: orchid_map_v1.xlsx (stub), network_peering_template.yaml (stub)]

Subject: Re: POC next steps — MAP and connectivity items

Looping in a couple of operational checks from the Dedicated/Private playbooks:
- TLS cert boundary: if Orchid expects mutual TLS on the peering tunnel, we need cert details before peering acceptance.
- API key scope: for cost isolation please confirm whether you want token limits by token-call-count or total token budget. We recommend token-budget quotas for PoCs.
- Network test plan: suggest two validation scripts: (1) streaming echo test (10–50 concurrent streams) and (2) KV-cache warmup (sample prompt set). We can provide runnable curl/python snippets.

Marissa
Program Manager, Customer Onboarding
Redwood Inference
